page.layout: One page of text. Marginal notes in the left margin (one reference, then a note of three fragments at the lower left). Running head at the top. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: Hebraica, in Chaldaicam linguam, anno ante natum Christum, circiter 40.

Circa hoc idem tempus, Simeon Hilleles, doctor in schola Hierosolymitana, ille qui (vt scribitur) Christū excepit in vlnas, egregia quædam scripsit. Post hunc, ipse etiam Gamaliel, Simeonis fi non filius, saltem discipulus (vocatur enim BenSimeon) legis explanationes edidit, ad cuius etiam pedes institutus fuit Apostolus Paulus.

Act.22.Omnes hos commentarios, & S. Bibliorum, legisq; Domini explicationes, Hebraei Graeca voce, appellarunt [illegible, ~9 letters]. Cæterum nihil horum scriptorum agnitum fuit aut receptum ab Ecclesia pro θεοπνεύστῳ[?].

Tandem igitur venit Iohannes Baptista: mox Christus: horum neuter quippiam scripsit: sed Euangelium utrque voce tantum prædicauit. Ac proprie Ioannes quidem Baptista Christum venisse, præsentem esse, non tam verbis, quam digito etiam demonstrauit. Christus vero Euangelium ita prædicauit, vt etiam quæ fuerant à Prophetis de se prædicta, reipsa compleuerit: atque ita adimpleuerit, vt nihil reliquerit vel dicendum, vel adimplendum. Huc illud Ioan.15[?]. Omnia quæcunque audiui à Patre, nota fecI vobis. Item illud, Matth.5[?]. Iota vnum, aut vnus apex non præteribit a lege, donec omnia fiant.
Christus[?] ur nil ripserit.Euangelij vero doctrinam à se prædicatam, miraculis permultis & manifestis confirmauit. Cur autem Christus nil

page.notes: Page number read as 112, the top figure is faint and may be 111 or 112. Running head "DE SACRA" at the top of the page. The Greek word after "appellarunt" is too worn to read letter by letter, so it is marked illegible. The Greek after "pro" is a best reading (θεοπνεύστῳ) and is marked [?]. The verse references "Ioan.15" and "Matth.5" are only partly legible and are marked [?]. The left margin fragments "Christus / ur nil / ripserit" are cut off at the edge and are read as one note with [?] on the first word. A faint show-through mark at the bottom ("M", "Hebr") is left out.
